articles.title: Ethereum
stale: The upgrade table ends at Pectra (May 2025). Fusaka activated on 3 December 2025, with PeerDAS (EIP-7594) and blob-parameter-only forks, and should be listed as of October 2026.
'Validators must deposit 32 ETH' is outdated. Since Pectra (EIP-7251), 32 ETH is the activation minimum and the maximum effective balance is 2,048 ETH for compounding (0x02) validators.
'Two kinds of accounts: EOAs ... and contract accounts' ignores EIP-7702 (Pectra), which lets EOAs set delegated code. The clean EOA/contract split no longer holds.
missing: State and execution internals: Merkle-Patricia state trie, state growth, statelessness/Verkle or binary-tree plans, and the execution/consensus client split via the Engine API
MEV and block building: proposer-builder separation via mev-boost/relays, ePBS (EIP-7732), censorship and inclusion lists (FOCIL)
Monetary policy and the post-Fusaka roadmap: issuance curve vs stake, net supply since Dencun, gas-limit increases, blob throughput targets and Glamsterdam
articles.notes: A readable, mostly accurate general overview at the level of a short Wikipedia intro. It stops at Pectra, and it is thin on the technical subjects protocol engineers care about: state, MEV, the client architecture and the roadmap.

articles.title: BNB
stale: Validators 'take turns producing blocks every few seconds': BSC block time was cut from 3 s to 1.5 s by the Lorentz hard fork (April 2025) and to about 0.75 s by Maxwell (mid-2025), so 'every few seconds' is out of date.

'The two chains were merged under the name BNB Chain in 2022': 2022 was a rebrand only. Binance Chain became BNB Beacon Chain, and it was actually retired via the BNB Chain Fusion (BC Fusion) migration in 2024, which moved staking and governance onto BSC. The article never mentions the Beacon Chain sunset.

Governance says BEPs are 'BNB Chain Evolution Proposals' voted by validators and stakers, which still reads like the pre-Fusion dual-chain setup. After 2024, staking and governance run in BSC system contracts (native staking, on-chain governance).
missing: PoSA internals: validator-set size and election per epoch, the Parlia engine, BEP-126 fast finality and slashing rules
BSC's MEV/proposer-builder market (BEP-322 builder API) and how centralized block building works in practice

articles.notes: Covers history and regulation (plea deal, SEC dismissal, pardon) accurately but is thin on mechanics. Consensus gets one sentence, and chain parameters (block time, Beacon Chain sunset) are out of date for 2026.

articles.title: Bitcoin Cash
stale: The 15 May 2026 'CashVM' row credits big-integer arithmetic to the 2026 upgrade, but the VM-limits and high-precision (BigInt) arithmetic CHIPs activated in the May 2025 upgrade. The 2026 upgrade added loops, functions, bitwise ops and pay-to-script, and the 2025 upgrade is missing from the table.
The history leaves the block size at the May 2018 32 MB cap. Since May 2024, BCH uses the Adaptive Blocksize Limit Algorithm (ABLA) with 32 MB as the floor, so 'larger blocks' is now a dynamic limit.
missing: Consensus-level differences in detail: SIGHASH_FORKID replay protection, the 2017 EDA difficulty chaos and the ASERT (aserti3-2d) algorithm, CTOR, and the ABLA block-size algorithm
Script/VM evolution: 2022 native introspection opcodes, CashTokens design (token prefix, fungible vs NFT capabilities) and what CashVM enables for contracts
Security analysis: hash-rate share vs Bitcoin, the 2018 hash war and checkpoint/rolling-finality debates, 51% attack cost, and the 0-conf/double-spend-proof story
articles.notes: A tidy overview with a correct core timeline. But 'How it works' is a two-sentence diff against Bitcoin, and the 2025/2026 upgrade contents appear to be mixed up.

articles.title: Cryptocurrency in Russia
stale: It says crypto is classified as 'property or digital financial assets'. Under Federal Law 259-FZ (2020), crypto is 'digital currency'; 'digital financial assets' (DFAs) are a separate category of tokenised rights issued on Central Bank-registered platforms. The article blurs the two.

The mining section omits the actual 2024 framework. Federal Law 221-FZ (effective 1 November 2024) legalised mining with a Ministry of Digital Development registry for companies and individual entrepreneurs, plus a household energy threshold for individuals. Regional mining bans took effect from 1 January 2025 in about 10 regions and run to 2031. 'Implementation varies by region' understates this.
Cross-border crypto settlement is attributed to the 2026 law. The experimental legal regime for cross-border crypto payments dates from September 2024 (Federal Law 223-FZ).
missing: Named statutes and dates: 259-FZ (2020), 221-FZ and 223-FZ (2024 mining and cross-border EPR), the 2025–2026 Bank of Russia concept, and the number and dates of the 2026 law

Concrete figures: personal and corporate tax rates on crypto (13–15% NDFL brackets, 25% corporate), VAT exemption, investor purchase caps for non-qualified investors, licensing deadlines and penalties

Sanctions-era enforcement and infrastructure: Garantex takedown (March 2025) and successor Grinex, the A7A5 ruble stablecoin, OFAC and EU sanctions on Russian crypto actors, and the digital ruble rollout
articles.notes: Vague, hedged boilerplate with almost no statute numbers, figures or named events. It conflates DFAs with digital currency, and two footnote references are broken across lines ('[^\ncbr]', '[^\n taxatlas]'). A specialist would not rely on it.

articles.title: Fiat currency
stale: Implies that the 1971 end of dollar-gold convertibility left most major currencies floating. Generalized floating began only in 1973, after the Smithsonian Agreement collapsed.

Describes the US as having 'an inflation-targeting framework in recent decades'. The Fed adopted an explicit 2% target only in 2012, moved to flexible average inflation targeting in 2020, and revised that framework again in August 2025.
Lists reserve requirements as a live tool without noting that the Fed set them to zero in March 2020 and operates an ample-reserves regime with interest on reserve balances as its main tool.
missing: How most fiat money is actually created: commercial bank lending and deposit creation (endogenous money), against the textbook money multiplier
Deeper history and theory: Song/Yuan paper money, colonial and Civil War greenbacks, and chartalism/MMT against metallism
Links to crypto: dollar stablecoins as fiat claims, CBDC status (digital euro, e-CNY), and Bitcoin's fixed-supply critique, with citations
articles.notes: A generic, essentially unsourced economics overview that reads like a textbook summary. It is acceptable as background but gives no mechanism detail and contains a few imprecise historical and policy claims.

articles.title: Litecoin

MWEB internals: peg-in/peg-out, the HogEx (integrating) transaction, cut-through, stealth addresses and non-interactive transactions (LIP-0003/0004), and its exchange and wallet support

Staking economics: adaptive issuance, the stake/delegate split, slashing for double-baking, and the minimum baker stake

Post-quantum signature trade-offs for Bitcoin: sizes and verification costs of ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FN-DSA and hash-based schemes (Lamport/Winternitz, SHRINCS), and their effect on block weight and the witness discount
Grover's impact on SHA-256 mining and hash-locked outputs, and rescue schemes for exposed coins such as ZK/STARK proofs of BIP-32 seed knowledge or commit-reveal spends
articles.notes: Carefully sourced and well scoped: the exposure table, long- versus short-exposure attacks, and the BIP-360/BIP-361 summaries are strong. articles.title: AssumeUTXO
stale: Says the snapshot is identified by a MuHash. Bitcoin Core's assumeutxo parameters (m_assumeutxo_data / AssumeutxoHash) use the SHA256-based hash_serialized (renamed hash_serialized_3 after the October 2023 bug fix), not MuHash. MuHash (#19055) is a separate gettxoutsetinfo option.
The 1,100 MiB prune-budget figure and the '2026 draft BIP for P2P UTXO-set sharing' are presented without a precise source and should be checked against the current doc/assumeutxo.md and Optech.
missing: How snapshot heights and hashes get chosen and reproduced at release time (contrib/devtools/utxo_snapshot.sh, reviewer reproduction), and the snapshot file size and format
Requirement that the headers chain must contain the base block before loading, and how the node handles a snapshot base on a stale or invalid fork
Resource cost of running two chainstates (dbcache split, disk, CPU) and how to measure time-to-usable against full IBD
articles.notes: The strongest article in this batch: a sourced step-by-step design, a release table, a clear trust model and practical RPC notes. The main error is calling the snapshot hash a MuHash.

articles.title: Bitcoin exchange-traded funds
stale: Says VanEck HODL's first trading day was 10 January 2024. All eleven approved spot products, HODL included, began trading on 11 January 2024, so this looks like the fund's commencement or launch date in its filing, not a trading date.
missing: How arbitrage keeps prices in line: NAV and iNAV calculation, the benchmark fixing window, and premium or discount behaviour
Tax and accounting treatment (grantor trust, 1099 reporting, wash-sale and in-kind tax implications) and how flows and holdings are tracked
Non-US products and comparisons (European ETPs and ETNs, Canadian, Hong Kong and Australian funds), plus the futures-ETF roll cost against spot
articles.notes: Heavily sourced from primary SEC filings, with a good history, creation and redemption mechanics, a custody section and balanced criticism. It lacks premium/arbitrage mechanics and non-US coverage.

articles.title: Cryptocurrency regulation and tax in India
stale: Cites 'section 285BAA' as the crypto-reporting provision in force from 1 April 2026. That is 1961-Act numbering, and the 1961 Act was repealed on that same date, so the operative provision should be cited by its Income-tax Act 2025 section number.
